\section[l'aumento]{l'aumento — the rise, the increase; the pay rise}

\label{lesson:IT-C361-aumento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the extension, then the Italian for the delivery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'aumento}
\textbf{l'aumento} — \textquotedblleft{}the rise, the increase; the pay rise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho chiesto un aumento al mio capo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I asked my boss for a pay rise.}
\end{quote}

\emph{In aumento} — rising: \emph{i prezzi sono in aumento}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aumento} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{augmentum} \textquotedblleft{}an increase, growth\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{augēre} \textquotedblleft{}to increase\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'aumento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'aumento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the extension, then the Italian for the delivery, then say \emph{l'aumento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la qualifica]{la qualifica — the qualification; the job title}

\label{lesson:IT-C361-qualifica}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the delivery, then the Italian for the rise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la qualifica}
\textbf{la qualifica} — \textquotedblleft{}the qualification; the job title\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Per questo lavoro serve una qualifica tecnica.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{For this job you need a technical qualification.}
\end{quote}

Stress: \emph{qualìfica}. On a contract it is your grade or title.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qualifica} is built on \emph{qualificare}, a learned borrowing from Medieval Latin \emph{quālificāre} \textquotedblleft{}to give a quality to\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{quālis} \textquotedblleft{}of what kind\textquotedblright{} and \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la qualifica}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la qualifica}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la qualifica}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the delivery, then the Italian for the rise, then say \emph{la qualifica} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la competenza]{la competenza — the skill, the competence}

\label{lesson:IT-C361-competenza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the rise, then the Italian for the qualification.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la competenza}
\textbf{la competenza} — \textquotedblleft{}the skill, the competence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ha grandi competenze in matematica.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She has great skills in mathematics.}
\end{quote}

Often plural: \emph{le competenze} on a CV. \emph{Non è di mia competenza} — it is not my area.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{competenza} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{competentia} \textquotedblleft{}agreement, fitness\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{competere} \textquotedblleft{}to meet, to be suitable\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{petere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la competenza}, once more

\end{itemize}

\section[la formazione]{la formazione — the training, the education; the line-up}

\label{lesson:IT-C361-formazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the qualification, then the Italian for the skill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la formazione}
\textbf{la formazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the training, the education; the line-up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'azienda offre un mese di formazione ai nuovi dipendenti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The company offers new employees a month of training.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La formazione} of a team is its line-up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{formazione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{fōrmātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a forming, a shaping\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{fōrma} \textquotedblleft{}shape, form\textquotedblright{}: training gives a shape.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il consulente]{il consulente — the consultant, the adviser}

\label{lesson:IT-C361-consulente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the skill, then the Italian for the training.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il consulente}
\textbf{il consulente} — \textquotedblleft{}the consultant, the adviser\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Abbiamo chiamato un consulente per organizzare il lavoro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We called in a consultant to organise the work.}
\end{quote}

One form for a man or a woman. \emph{Consulenza} is the advice or the service.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{consulente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cōnsulēns}, present participle of \emph{cōnsulere} \textquotedblleft{}to take counsel, to consult\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
